articles.originalTitle: Black Wall Street Journey: Re and De Imagining Black Progress: Rick Lowe | Museum Exhibitions | News - Gagosian
articles.title: Rick Lowe's Largest Institutional Solo Exhibition Opens at the University of Michigan
articles.excerpt: Rick Lowe's largest institutional solo exhibition in the United States, Black Wall Street Journey, opens at the University of Michigan Museum of Art. The show combines art, data, and research to examine community prosperity.
articles.content: Marking Rick Lowe's largest institutional solo exhibition in the United States, Black Wall Street Journey opened at the University of Michigan Museum of Art. Running from September 26, 2026, to January 24, 2027, the exhibition brings together painting, sculpture, and public installation. The project is the culmination of the artist's three-year residency at the university's Institute for Social Research. Developed in collaboration with researchers, data scientists, and students, the work examines forces shaping wealth and opportunity across income, education, housing, and business ownership. In other developments, Adriana Varejão is preparing to represent Brazil at the 61st Biennale di Venezia with a presentation curated by Diane Lima, placing her in conversation with artist Rosana Paulino. Varejão's exhibition, titled Comigo ninguém pode, is installed within the Brazilian Pavilion's modernist structure.

articles.originalTitle: Glenn Brown in: Fail We May, Sail We Must | Museum Exhibitions | News - Gagosian
articles.title: Glenn Brown Collection Opens New Exhibition in London
articles.excerpt: Curated by Glenn Brown and Edgar Laguinia, the exhibition Fail We May, Sail We Must has opened at the Brown Collection in London, bringing together works by more than twenty artists.
articles.content: The Brown Collection has launched the exhibition titled Fail We May, Sail We Must, on view through August 7, 2027. Curated by Glenn Brown and collection cofounder Edgar Laguinia, the presentation features historic and contemporary paintings, sculptures, drawings, prints, and ceramics by more than twenty artists. The selection highlights how art spanning six centuries can challenge the mind and forge new connections between works not typically seen together, including pieces by Brown himself. In parallel developments, the Fall 2026 issue of Gagosian Quarterly is now available alongside a new catalogue dedicated to Brice Marden. Additionally, artist Adriana Varejão is preparing a series of new paintings and sculptures to represent Brazil at the 61st Biennale di Venezia. Curated by Diane Lima, her exhibition titled Comigo ninguém pode places her in dialogue with Rosana Paulino to reflect on colonial history and the rewriting of the past within the Brazilian Pavilion's Modernist structure.

articles.originalTitle: Switzerland’s Fondation Beyeler opens £109.7m expansion - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: Basel's Fondation Beyeler Opens £109.7m Expansion Designed by Peter Zumthor
articles.excerpt: Switzerland's Fondation Beyeler in Basel is launching a £109.7m expansion featuring three new structures by architect Peter Zumthor and doubled parkland, implementing a controlled opening period for visitors.
articles.content: The Fondation Beyeler in Basel, Switzerland, is opening a major expansion project costing approximately SFr 120m, introducing three new structures designed by Swiss architect Peter Zumthor alongside an expanded park area. Funded largely by Swiss entrepreneur Hansjörg Wyss, the primary new gallery building increases the museum's exhibition space by 1,500 sq. m. The expansion also features the freestanding Ammann Pavilion for recitals and performances, and the Erlen Torhaus, which adds office space to an 18th-century villa on the property. Furthermore, the surrounding parkland has doubled to nearly 20,000 sq. m, incorporating new sculptural installations. An exhibition titled Constellations, running until 5 September 2027, connects works across the museum's original Renzo Piano spaces and the new galleries. Eschewing a traditional large celebration, the institution has scheduled a controlled inauguration period from 26 September to 14 January 2027, reducing visitor numbers and opening days to carefully observe and optimize operations based on visitor patterns.

articles.originalTitle: K-art, William Kentridge and a Turner prize worth getting excited for – the week in art - The Guardian
articles.title: Turner Prize Exhibition Opens in Middlesbrough Featuring Diverse Shortlisted Artists
articles.excerpt: The 2026 Turner Prize exhibition at MIMA in Middlesbrough brings together works by Kira Freije, Simeon Barclay, Tanoa Sasraku, and Marguerite Humeau.
articles.content: Opening at MIMA in Middlesbrough, the 2026 Turner Prize exhibition showcases works by shortlisted artists including Kira Freije, who constructs a waste land populated by Rodinesque figures, alongside Simeon Barclay exploring masculinity, Tanoa Sasraku addressing big oil, and Marguerite Humeau. The exhibition runs from 26 September through 29 March. Meanwhile, the British Museum prepares to launch a survey spanning 2,000 years of Korean art, belief, and philosophy from 1 October until 31 January. In London, Mark Wallinger's paintings and film exploring abstraction remain on view at the Paul Stolper Gallery until 24 October, while the Goodman Gallery presents a new animated film by William Kentridge through 7 November. Additionally, Rembrandt's depiction of Paul at the National Gallery continues to draw attention for its profound engagement with the human condition and suffering.

articles.originalTitle: The astonishing story of Van Gogh collector Gertrud Dübi-Müller is finally celebrated in an exhibition at Switzerland’s Kunstmuseum Basel - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: Art Collector Gertrud Dübi-Müller's Life Celebrated at Kunstmuseum Basel
articles.excerpt: Kunstmuseum Basel is hosting an exhibition celebrating the life and pioneering art collecting of Gertrud Dübi-Müller, who purchased a Van Gogh portrait as a teenager in 1908.
articles.content: The life and collecting journey of Swiss pioneer Gertrud Dübi-Müller are the focus of an exhibition at the Kunstmuseum Basel. Inheriting wealth from her family's engineering business after being orphaned at a young age, Müller acquired Vincent van Gogh's Portrait of Charles-Elzéard Trabuc in 1908 when she was only 19 years old. This purchase predated widespread international recognition for the artist and sparked considerable enthusiasm among her avant-garde circle, including artists Cuno Amiet and Giovanni Giacometti. Alongside her early art acquisitions, Müller led an adventurous life, becoming the first woman in Solothurn to own a car. She later married lawyer Otto Dübi in 1921 and maintained her dedication to modern art throughout her life. Upon her death in 1980, Dübi-Müller bequeathed 190 works to the Kunstmuseum Solothurn, including pieces by Paul Cezanne, Henri Matisse, and Pablo Picasso alongside works by her Swiss artist friends. The exhibition runs until 7 February 2027, highlighting her remarkable early acquisition and her enduring engagement with modern art.

articles.originalTitle: ‘It is not a political joke’: Ai Weiwei unveils 500 cast-iron combat helmets in Sydney - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: Ai Weiwei Unveils 500 Cast-Iron Combat Helmets Installation in Sydney
articles.excerpt: Chinese contemporary artist Ai Weiwei has unveiled "Mushrooms" in Sydney, a public artwork comprising 500 cast-iron combat helmets that reflects on nations' inadequate responses to global crises.
articles.content: Chinese contemporary artist Ai Weiwei has unveiled his latest work, titled "Mushrooms," outside the Museum of Contemporary Art Australia in Sydney. On view for seven months, the artwork comprises 500 cast-iron combat helmets arranged in ten uniform rows. According to the artist, the title references growth in darkness, nuclear mushroom clouds, and connotations of endless delays in Chinese. The concept originated when Germany offered 5,000 helmets to aid Ukraine in early 2022, a response widely criticized as feeble. Clarifying that the piece is not a political joke, the artist stated that the work demonstrates the shallow understanding modern national leadership holds regarding the human condition and future uncertainties. Pointing to both armed conflicts and the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence as challenges to traditional human value systems, the artist emphasized that speaking out on human rights and freedom of expression remains a vital form of human resistance.

articles.originalTitle: Why Toronto is fast becoming unmissable for art - artbasel.com
articles.title: Toronto's Expanding Art Scene and New Infrastructure Initiatives
articles.excerpt: Kenneth Montague, founder of The Wedge Collection, notes that Toronto's hybrid identity rooted in a majority immigrant population forms the foundation of the city's contemporary art scene.
articles.content: With 51 percent of its population born abroad, Toronto's cultural hybridity underpins its growing arts ecosystem. This diversity was highlighted at the Venice Biennale, which featured artists such as Alexa Kumiko Hatanaka, Rajni Perera, Abbas Akhavan, and Manuel Mathieu. Currently in its fourth edition, the Toronto Biennial, curated by Allison Glenn under the title Things Fall Apart, examines shared geographies along the Great Lakes across venues ranging from a Sikh Gurdwara to the St George Subway Station and the Aga Khan Museum. Along the waterfront in the revitalized Port Lands district, the Lassonde Art Trail has opened with 17 new commissions supported by a CAD 25 million seed grant from philanthropist Pierre Lassonde. The trail features a major public sculpture by Kent Monkman. Meanwhile, artists like Rajni Perera and Nirbhai Singh Sidhu are establishing independent studio and exhibition spaces, while established institutions such as the Art Gallery of Ontario and MOCA continue to expand their facilities and programming for the city's visual arts community.

articles.originalTitle: Ai Weiwei unveils his epic new Australian work: ‘90% of art is just garbage. Real art questions the existing order’ - The Guardian
articles.title: Ai Weiwei Unveils New Monumental Sculpture Installation on Sydney Harbour
articles.excerpt: Artist Ai Weiwei has unveiled Mushrooms, a 40-metre-long installation focused on the themes of war and combat helmets outside Sydney's Museum of Contemporary Art.
articles.content: Living on his farm in Portugal, artist Ai Weiwei has unveiled his latest large-scale installation titled Mushrooms, displayed on the Tallawoladah Lawn outside Sydney's Museum of Contemporary Art. The work measures 40 metres in length and features 500 identical cast-iron sculptures of combat helmets arranged on an elevated platform. The title draws a visual connection between mushroom caps and the shape of military helmets, while also invoking associations with decay, death, and the fragility of life exposed by armed conflict. Ai stated that the origins of the commission trace back to his 2015 documentary Human Flow, which led him to study contemporary warfare and the mechanics of munitions. Reflecting on the early stages of the Russia-Ukraine conflict, he recalled Germany offering 5,000 helmets to Ukraine. Having visited Ukrainian soldiers on the frontline four times last year, the artist sought to highlight the realities of war against a backdrop overlooking the Sydney Opera House. Critiquing the contemporary art world, Ai asserted that the majority of museum works are decorative rather than connected to human struggle, maintaining that real art must question the existing order.

articles.originalTitle: Major Retrospective of Sri Lankan Architect Geoffrey Bawa Opens at the Vitra Design Museum - Architectural Record
articles.title: Sri Lankan Architect Geoffrey Bawa Celebrated in Major Retrospective
articles.excerpt: The Vitra Design Museum hosts the first major Geoffrey Bawa retrospective in over 20 years, examining the architect's five-decade career through drawings, models, and archival documents.
articles.content: Recognized as one of the most influential architects in 20th-century Asia, Sri Lankan-born Geoffrey Bawa's illustrious five-decade career is the subject of a major retrospective at the Vitra Design Museum in Weil am Rhein, Germany. Running from September 26 through February 28, 2027, the exhibition titled Geoffrey Bawa: Architecture for the Senses features more than 250 drawings, models, photographs, furniture pieces, and archival documents. Organized by the Vitra Design Museum, M+, and the Wüstenrot Foundation in collaboration with the Geoffrey Bawa Trust, the showcase spans diverse projects such as the Bentota Beach Hotel, the Kandalama Hotel, and his country estate Lunuganga. Newly commissioned photographs by Iwan Baan highlight the buildings' close relationships with their surrounding landscapes. The retrospective emphasizes Bawa's integration of terrain, rocks, and vegetation into spatial sequences, as well as his collaborations with Sri Lankan artists and craftspeople including Laki Senanayake, Ena de Silva, and Barbara Sansoni. Featuring scenography by Lebanese architect Lina Ghotmeh, the exhibition will travel to M+ in Hong Kong in June 2027 following its German presentation.

articles.originalTitle: Herzog & de Meuron reuses foundations for mass-timber Massachusetts school building - Dezeen
articles.title: Herzog & de Meuron Reuses Existing Foundations for Massachusetts College Building
articles.excerpt: Swiss architecture studio Herzog & de Meuron has utilised existing concrete foundations for a new Student Center and Dining Commons at Amherst College, incorporating mass-timber levels and deep solar-shading eaves.
articles.content: Swiss architecture studio Herzog & de Meuron has utilised the existing concrete foundation of an older structure for the Student Center and Dining Commons at Amherst College in Massachusetts, expanding the building from 80,000 to 120,000 square feet. Working alongside executive architect Sasaki, the studio preserved two lower-level foundations of the former Merrill Science Center to navigate the sloped site and align with the institution's carbon neutrality goals. Two upper levels constructed primarily from Canadian Black Spruce mass timber were added atop the skeleton, featuring light-oiled Western Red Cedar cladding above and dark-stained timber on the lower levels. The structural design connects mass-timber columns directly to pre-existing concrete supports using split-beam and corbel joints. The third level accommodates study and event spaces alongside a winter garden courtyard, while the roof holds low-lying pavilions containing a black-box theatre and solar panel arrays. According to the studio, the design achieves a 33 per cent reduction in embodied carbon and a 93 per cent reduction in operational carbon compared to conventional building types. This project marks Herzog & de Meuron's first completed educational building in the United States.

articles.originalTitle: Architectural Details: Snider House Bridges Past and Present - Architizer
articles.title: Giannone Petricone Associates Revitalizes 1828 Snider House in North Toronto
articles.excerpt: Giannone Petricone Associates has restored and updated Snider House, North Toronto's oldest surviving building, blending historic design with a glass addition.
articles.content: Giannone Petricone Associates has restored and revitalized Snider House, identified as the oldest surviving building in North Toronto. Originally built in 1828 in the Regency style, the landmark was upgraded to modern standards while preserving its historic character. The original Regency cottage façade maintains its formal, symmetrical presence at the front, while a contemporary rear glass extension opens the dwelling to the landscape. Co-founding principal Pina Petricone notes that the firm approaches heritage projects to celebrate distinct attributes through contrast and layering. The standout architectural feature at the rear is an undulating, two-story glass façade. Fabricated using a gravity-curved method on hot sand beds in Spain and combined with low-E insulated glass technology, this custom curtain wall contrasts with the heavy clay brick of the original structure. Inside, the restored interior balances heritage formality with material restraint, maintaining warmth in the dining and sitting rooms. The kitchen and adjoining living areas open fully to the backyard. Reimagined wide baseboards function simultaneously as visual accents and air diffusers, helping the historic home meet contemporary standards.

articles.originalTitle: Fondation Beyeler Expands with Three New Buildings by Peter Zumthor - ArchDaily
articles.title: Fondation Beyeler Expands with Three New Buildings by Peter Zumthor
articles.excerpt: Switzerland's Fondation Beyeler is expanding its museum ensemble with three new structures by architect Peter Zumthor, an enlarged park, and restored historic buildings ahead of its full opening.
articles.content: The Fondation Beyeler in Riehen, Switzerland, is expanding its museum ensemble with three new buildings designed by Swiss architect Peter Zumthor, an enlarged park, and restored historic structures. Extending the existing museum designed by Renzo Piano, the expansion adds exhibition, education, cultural, and public spaces while opening a previously private section of the surrounding landscape to visitors. The expanded ensemble will begin welcoming visitors on September 26, 2026, during a preview phase before its full opening on January 15, 2027. Zumthor's additions comprise the Wyss Museum, the Ammann Pavilion, and the Erlen Torhaus. The three-storey Wyss Museum adds approximately 1,500 square meters of exhibition space and is constructed largely using locally quarried Jura limestone. Positioned between the structures, the Ammann Pavilion acts as a public gathering space, while the timber-frame Erlen Torhaus forms a transition between the urban fabric and the adjacent nature reserve. Landscape forms an integral part of the expansion, with the addition of nearly 10,000 square meters of formerly private parkland nearly doubling the size of Beyeler Park. The expanded park incorporates existing and new works by prominent artists. Several historic buildings, including the Orangerie and Ammann Atelier, have also been restored and adapted for art education, botany, and cultural projects.

articles.originalTitle: Bigger Isn't Just an Aesthetic Choice: What Façade Systems Conceal Behind Their Materials - ArchDaily
articles.title: Aesthetics and Material Performance in Large-Format Façade Systems
articles.excerpt: As minimal joints and seamless surfaces define contemporary architecture, large-format panels introduce new technical approaches regarding durability, recyclability, and structural performance.
articles.content: While contemporary architecture favors clean lines and minimal joints, increasing panel dimensions influences durability, recyclability, and external performance. To counter the risk of surface waviness in thin sheets, the building industry has traditionally relied on aluminum composite materials with plastic cores, which introduce recycling challenges. Alternatively, monomaterial systems utilize structural stiffeners integrated directly into a single aluminum sheet, providing mechanical stiffness without a composite core. This design eliminates the risk of delamination and supports full material recyclability. Engineered to withstand high wind loads and impact requirements, such panel systems streamline construction through sequential installation methods. Weather-tight fasteners and interlocking drainage systems ensure long-term performance, demonstrating how monomaterial façades balance architectural expression with environmental considerations.

articles.originalTitle: About the Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires exhibition - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: V&A Museum Announces Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires Exhibition
articles.excerpt: The Victoria and Albert Museum will open Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires on 7 November 2026, exploring 16 centuries of artistic production between AD 330 and 1922.
articles.content: The Victoria and Albert Museum in South Kensington has announced a new exhibition titled Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires, opening on 7 November 2026. The exhibition explores 1,600 years of artistic production from AD 330 to 1922, tracing the enduring creative legacy of an imperial capital that shaped the Mediterranean world and beyond. Spanning the Byzantine and Ottoman empires, the showcase features more than 200 objects across four main sections. These include rarely seen decorative arts, textiles, ceramic tiles, mosaics, precious metalwork, manuscripts, and paintings. The sections trace the city from its refounding under Constantine the Great to its role as a religious and administrative center. Grand Beginnings highlights the infrastructure and Hippodrome of the early capital, while Heaven and Earth examines Byzantine sacred imagery and classical art. Power and Reach investigates Ottoman court authority through visual spectacle and luxury materials. Finally, Life in the City explores religious coexistence, urban leisure, and 19th-century shifts in fashion and design. The exhibition concludes by examining the influence of Byzantine and Ottoman art on 19th-century European creators.

articles.originalTitle: peter zumthor's expanded fondation beyeler opens to the public - Designboom
articles.title: Peter Zumthor's Expanded Fondation Beyeler Opens to the Public
articles.excerpt: Peter Zumthor's expansion of the Fondation Beyeler in Riehen begins its opening to the public, gradually revealing new buildings and parkland from September 2026.
articles.content: Peter Zumthor's expansion of the Fondation Beyeler in Riehen near Basel is opening to the public, with the new ensemble gradually revealed from September 26, 2026, ahead of its full opening in January 2027. Selected unanimously by an international jury, Zumthor divided the new functions between three distinct buildings—the Wyss Museum, the Ammann Pavilion, and the Erlen Torhaus—to avoid a single bulky structure. The Wyss Museum adds approximately 1,500 square meters of exhibition space across three floors, featuring an irregular Y-shaped plan and a hand-built Jura limestone rammed-concrete facade. The single-story glass and oak Ammann Pavilion functions as a public lounge during the day and hosts cultural events in the evening. Furthermore, the architectural expansion is accompanied by the opening of nearly 10,000 square meters of formerly private 19th-century parkland to visitors, integrating meadows, native orchids, and water features into the museum grounds.

articles.originalTitle: Standout Collectible Designs at Paris Design Week 2026 - WWD
articles.title: Standout Collectible Designs Unveiled at Paris Design Week
articles.excerpt: The 16th edition of Paris Design Week showcased contemporary collections rooted in traditional techniques and natural forms.
articles.content:
Paris Design Week concluded its 16th edition with showrooms across Saint-Germain-des-Prés and beyond displaying contemporary decor from 500 exhibitors. Draga & Aurel showcased their Crisalide side tables at Galerie BSL, combining fused colored glass and brass bases. Pinto collaborated with fabric firm Nobilis to present the Foundation collection, featuring warm tones and jacquard motifs. Yves Salomon Éditions unveiled Tactile Monuments, its first complete interior collection centered on merino shearling and natural volumes.

Swedish design house Veermakers opened its inaugural Paris showroom in Le Marais to highlight Scandinavian craftsmanship. Nordic Knots presented wool rugs inspired by Swedish Grace, while lifestyle brand L'Objet partnered with jeweler Jessica McCormack on a marine-themed home collection. Modern Metier debuted Tropic of Capricorn, created with French designer Rudy Guénaire. Garnier & Linker introduced Aurora, its first outdoor lighting collection in cast aluminum. Franck Genser presented sculptural furniture including his Piscine VI coffee table, and cousins Cédric and Nicolas Hervet exhibited their woodworking collection spanning living and dining spaces.

articles.originalTitle: Sansetsukon x Es Devlin: MILK - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: Sansetsukon and Es Devlin to Present Live Performance at V&A East Storehouse
articles.excerpt: Dance collective Sansetsukon will present MILK, a live performance responding to Es Devlin’s installation The Everythingists, for free at the V&A East Storehouse on 3 October 2026.
articles.content: Dance collective Sansetsukon is preparing to stage MILK, a new live performance responding to Es Devlin’s installation The Everythingists. The event will take place on 3 October 2026 at Gallery 2 within the V&A East Storehouse. Scheduled for 2:00 PM, 5:00 PM, and 8:00 PM, each performance lasts between 25 and 30 minutes and is free to the public. Through dance, sound, light, and shadow, the performance creates a dialogue between the dancers, the installation, and the surrounding gallery space. The work draws inspiration from Rayonism and concepts regarding humans empowered by machines and machines empowered by artists. Performers move through the gallery to a soundscape created by reworking audio elements from The Everythingists. The ensemble features dancers Joshua Shanny-Wynter, Deavion Brown, Robbie Ordoña, Peter Butler, Tania Dimbelolo, Lois Samphier, and Anna Watanabe, with a musical composition by Serian Griffiths and sound design by Nana Nakashima.

articles.originalTitle: 200,000 young people and counting: Tate celebrates a new generation with landmark commission for young artists - tate.org.uk
articles.title: Tate Collective Reaches 200,000 Members and Launches Landmark Open Call
articles.excerpt: Tate Collective, the free membership scheme for 16 to 25-year-olds, has reached 200,000 members and launched an open call for a new artwork to be displayed at Tate Modern.
articles.content: Tate Collective, a free membership scheme for 16 to 25-year-olds, has reached a milestone of 200,000 members. To mark the occasion, an open call has been launched inviting members to create a new artwork for display at Tate Modern alongside figures such as Andy Warhol, Salvador Dalí, and Marina Abramović. The winning commission will be selected by a jury chaired by Rosalie Doubal and will go on display in March 2027, with submissions closing on 19 October. Concurrently, Tate Modern Lates is celebrating its 10th anniversary, having drawn 870,000 attendees over the past decade to after-hours events featuring live music, performances, and workshops. Karin Hindsbo, Interim Director of Tate, stated that the members represent a generation choosing to engage with art and ideas. The anniversary celebrations will culminate on 30 October with a special Late event programmed by Shygirl. Tate Collective membership offers various discounts and access to creative opportunities with support from patrons and foundations.

articles.originalTitle: Biennale College Architettura 2026/2027: the 12 selected projects - labiennale.org
articles.title: Twelve Projects Selected for Biennale College Architettura 2026-2027
articles.excerpt: Twelve projects have been selected for the third edition of Biennale College Architettura. The projects by practitioners under 30 will be developed during a workshop from 22 to 30 September 2026.
articles.content: Twelve projects have been selected for the 3rd edition of Biennale College Architettura 2026–2027. The emerging practitioners under 30 originate from China, Croatia, Italy, Mexico, Syria, Spain, Turkey, Tunisia, the USA, and Hungary. The initiative complements the 20th International Architecture Exhibition, titled Do Architecture and curated by Wang Shu and Lu Wenyu, serving as a research, experimentation, and production laboratory. The open call attracted over 80 emerging practitioners from 36 countries. The 12 selected projects are presented by Ahlem Balghouthi, Fabio Bari, Stav Bouzaglo, Antonino Caridi, Yiying Chen, Alejandro Ferrer Esplugues, Jin Gao, Nisa Gökgöz, Matej Orkić, Julia Polefko, Ahmad Salah, and Guillermo Sanchez Cardenas. The workshop will take place from 22 to 30 September 2026, coordinated by Wang Shu and Lu Wenyu alongside tutors. Following the workshop, up to four projects will be selected to receive a 25,000 euro grant for the realization of the final work, which will be presented out of competition during Biennale Architettura 2027.

articles.originalTitle: Art Basel Paris 2026 Press Dossier: a deep-dive into this year's highlights - artbasel.com
articles.title: Art Basel Paris 2026 Prepares With 211 Galleries and Expanded Spaces
articles.excerpt: Art Basel Paris is preparing to open with 211 galleries from 41 countries and regions. The fair features the relocation of Premise to the Salon Seine and an expanded public program around the Grand Palais.
articles.content: Art Basel Paris is bringing together leading representatives of modern and contemporary art with 211 galleries participating from 41 countries and regions. The event features 183 galleries in the Galeries sector, 16 in Emergence, and 12 in Premise. This year, the fair welcomes 32 first-time participants while moving the Premise sector to a larger space at Salon Seine. Sixty-four galleries operating in France take part in the roster, with galleries such as Petrine and The Pill graduating from Emergence into the main Galeries sector. The presentations feature works by Paris-based figures such as Pol Taburet, Julien Creuzet, Annie Ernaux, Tarek Lakhrissi, and Neïla Czermak Ichti, alongside a broad international roster of artists and galleries.

articles.originalTitle: ARTIST ROOMS: Robert Rauschenberg at Tate Modern, 21 September 2026 - December 2027 – Press Release - tate.org.uk
articles.title: Tate Modern Opens Large-Scale Robert Rauschenberg Display
articles.excerpt: Tate Modern is launching a large-scale free display of over 20 works by Robert Rauschenberg spanning three decades to mark the centenary of his birth.
articles.content: Tate Modern is launching a large-scale free display of works by Robert Rauschenberg, running from 21 September 2026 to December 2027. Marking the centenary of the artist's birth, the presentation brings together over 20 works spanning three decades, including paintings, prints, and kinetic installations. At the heart of the presentation are Glut sculptures, including three newly gifted by the Robert Rauschenberg Foundation to the Tate Americas Foundation. Curated by Gregor Muir, Andrew de Brún, and Julia Blaut, the display foregrounds Rauschenberg's engagement with dance and performance, featuring metal sculptures, performance sets, and costume designs. The exhibition is organized as part of the ARTIST ROOMS touring programme, jointly managed by Tate and the National Galleries of Scotland.

articles.originalTitle: Maison Michel Celebrates 90 Years of Hatmaking With New Exhibition at Chanel’s Le19M - WWD
articles.title: Maison Michel Celebrates 90th Anniversary With Paris Exhibition
articles.excerpt: Parisian hatmaker Maison Michel marks its 90th anniversary with a dedicated exhibition opening at La Galerie du 19M.
articles.content:
Parisian hatmaker Maison Michel is marking its 90th anniversary with an exhibition celebrating the journey from raw material to finished product. Part of Chanel's specialized workshop network since 1997, the house presents the display at La Galerie du 19M, Chanel's craftsmanship hub in northern Paris. Running from Sept. 23 until Dec. 13, the exhibition highlights ancient tools, techniques, and the work behind the designs.

Titled "Metamorphoses — The Hats of Maison Michel," the showcase begins with tree trunks carved into raw hat shapes alongside 4,000 wooden hat blocks from the archives. Curated by artistic director Priscilla Royer and Palais Galliera fashion museum director Emilie Hammen, the exhibition features specially commissioned artworks and runway designs. Maison Michel remains one of the few remaining producers mastering sewn straw, utilizing ancient sewing machines. The display explores headgear's evolution from social signifier to a form of personal expression, featuring items crafted from canvas, organza, leather, and tweed.
